title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. π_{0,3}^ is the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}. Π_{0,3}^ appears to be its extension by the S_3 symmetries, generated by an involution σ_∞ and an order-3 rotation ρ. ε_0 is the extra involution, so π^{~∧} = π^∧·{1, ε_0}. l_0 and l_1 are the inertia loops at 0 and 1. M^{!~}_{0,3} is a group of 'admissible' outer-type automorphisms of these groups. Each u is encoded by elements α, β (or f, η, g, h) via u(σ_∞) = int(α)σ_∞ and u(ρ) = int(β)ρ, as in (117)/(118) on the next page. The constraints form the 'relation des lacets' (loop equation).

Top of page (end of case 2). The automorphisms in question map, under μ, into the Borel-type subgroup {cρ+d} of GL(2,Ẑ) found on the previous page, i.e. u = u_{α,βf} with image μ(cρ+d). In this case δ = ε_3(u) = 1. These u correspond to pairs (η, f) satisfying:
- (111) η σ_∞(η) = 1, which is a 2-cycle relation;
- (111') f ρ(f)^{-1} = η l_1^ν.
The margin remarks that one can rewrite this in terms of (α, β) satisfying the loop relation, completed by f = α.

Case 3. This is the case f ≡ 1 mod L_0, where L_0 = l_0^{Ẑ} is the inertia subgroup at 0. Equivalently α and β are L_0-equivalent to the base solutions α_0, β_0. Then u(ε_0) = ε_0^μ with μ ∈ Ẑ^*, i.e. (114) [u, ε_0] = l_0^ν with ν = (μ−1)/2. Equivalently, u normalizes L_0' = ε_0^{Ẑ}, and L_0 = L_0' ∩ π_{0,3} (margin NB). There is a residual indeterminacy (α, β, f) ↦ (l_0^n α, l_0^n β, l_0^n f). It can be killed by imposing (115) f = 1, which fixes α and β uniquely.

Conclusion. The normalizer M^{!~}_{0,3}[0] of L_0 is in bijection with pairs (α, β), α ∈ π^{~∧}, β ∈ π^∧, satisfying the loop relations. The next page states these as g ρ(g) ρ²(g) = 1, h σ_∞(h) = 1, g = h l_1^ν.

In modern terms this is a profinite description of automorphisms preserving inertia at 0, given by a pair of a 2-cycle relation and a 3-cycle relation linked by a twist exponent. That is essentially the defining data of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT^ (Drinfeld 1990, Ihara), with the inertia-normalization step (killing the l_0^n ambiguity) and the relation μ = 2ν+1 (Drinfeld's λ = 2m+1).
errors: No clear mathematical error visible; the page is a bookkeeping step.

The claim that f = 1 'determines α, β uniquely' tacitly needs the centralizer of l_0 in π^∧ to be L_0 itself. This holds (inertia subgroups in free profinite groups are self-centralizing), but it is not stated.
In (114), ν = (μ−1)/2 requires μ to be odd in Ẑ; this is implicit from ε_0 being an involution / ε_3 conditions, but it is not argued here.

ideas.what: Encoding automorphisms of the S_3-symmetric profinite π_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}) by pairs (α, β) / (g, h) satisfying 2-cycle and 3-cycle 'loop' relations linked by a power of the inertia generator l_1
ideas.modern_name: Defining relations of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT^ (2-cycle and 3-cycle / hexagon-type relations)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara (1990–91); Grothendieck's program in Esquisse (1984)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme sketches the idea qualitatively; the explicit 'équation des lacets' appears in La Longue Marche notes (circulated, unpublished)

ideas.what: Normalizing the l_0^n ambiguity by imposing f = 1 for automorphisms that normalize the inertia L_0
ideas.modern_name: Normalization of GT elements (f chosen in the commutator subgroup / inertia-preserving lift)
Relation λ = 2m+1 between the cyclotomic character and the exponent m in GT

ideas.what: Subgroup of M^{!~}_{0,3} mapping to the Borel-type subgroup {cρ+d} of GL(2,Ẑ) (case 2)
ideas.modern_name: Image of the automorphism group in GL(2,Ẑ) acting on the abelianization of the modular-type group

missed.claim: Grothendieck already writes the twist relation μ = 2ν+1 (Drinfeld's λ = 2m+1) and the inertia normalization in an S_3-symmetric profinite setting. This predates Drinfeld's GT^ and is a concrete precursor; its exact credit in the literature is unclear.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical priority documentation for GT^-type relations in Grothendieck's 'équation des lacets' notes. The archive is now public, so specialists (Lochak, Schneps) may be partly aware.

deep.surprise_reason: Recognizably the GT-type 2-cycle/3-cycle relations with λ = 2m+1 and inertia normalization, worked out by Grothendieck before Drinfeld. However, the page itself is a routine case analysis, and the general fact that the Longue Marche notes contain the loop equation is known to experts.
transcription_corrections: (110) should read u = u_{α,β,f} ↦ μ(cρ+d) (the 'c' is missing in the transcription).
Margin under (114): '(agissant sur Π_{0,3}) u normalise L_0' = {ε_0^n | n ∈ Ẑ}', with left-margin 'NB L_0 = L_0' ∩ Π_{0,3}'.
Last line: α ∈ π_{0,3}^{~∧} = π_{0,3}^∧·{1, ε_0}, β ∈ π_{0,3}^∧ (the 'ε_0' may be written as a different symbol in the image).
